newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gross public debt ended '96 at 53 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gross public debt ended '96 at 53 pct/GDP.

text.p: Brazil's gross public sector debt ended 1996 at $394.72 billion, the equivalent of 53 percent of gross domestic product, the Central Bank said.

The Central Bank said in a report on the structure of public sector debt that gross internal debt by the end of last year reached $300.372 billion, or 40 percent of GDP, and gross external debt was $94.348 billion, or 13 percent of GDP.

The gross figure included debt contracted by all parts of the public sector. After subtracting reserves and other assets, the net public sector debt at the end of 1996 was $258.974 billion, equivalent to 34 percent of GDP, the bank said.
The report said a total of $7.198 billion in external debt would come due during 1997 and have to be retired. In 1996, $3.68 billion in external debt was retired.
In 1998, $7.509 billion in external debt will come due, in 1999 $6.624 billion and in the year 2000 $5.284 billion.

Of that, the Central Bank said 58 percent was paying fixed rate interest, 1.0 percent was paying the TJLP Long-Term Interest Rate and 11 percent was dollar-indexed. Eight percent was paying interest at the Reference Rate (TR), three percent was paying interest adjusted for IGP-M inflation and 19 percent was paying a set percentage over the Selic interest rate.
